audit_scope.description: This batch covers both EL and CL specifications: EVM storage instructions (SLOAD/SSTORE/TLOAD/TSTORE with gas economics), EVM arithmetic opcodes, gas repricing (EIP-2929 cold/warm access, EIP-7883 ModExp repricing), transaction gas caps (EIP-7825), CL validator activation churn limits (EIP-7514), pre-merge history expiry (EIP-7927), node configuration RPC (EIP-7910), and dapp transaction authorization (EIP-107).

in_scope: EVM Storage Instructions (SLOAD, SSTORE, TLOAD, TSTORE)
EVM Arithmetic Instructions (ADD, SUB, DIV, SDIV, MOD, SMOD, ADDMOD, MULMOD, EXP, SIGNEXTEND)
Gas Pricing (EIP-2929 cold/warm access lists, EIP-7883 ModExp repricing)
out_of_scope: Browser wallet UI details (EIP-107 popup rendering)

misclassified_entities.reason: Internal EVM component. A caller contract within the EVM execution context is part of the system under audit, not an external entity. The external entity is the user/EOA who initiates the transaction.

Internal EVM component. A smart contract calling a precompile operates within the EVM execution boundary. The true external entity is the transaction sender who constructed the calldata with ModExp inputs.
Internal component. The local Ethereum node is the system under audit itself, not an external entity.

trusted_external_entities.name: Validator Depositor via Deposit Contract
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Deposit Contract (32 ETH deposit with validator pubkey and withdrawal credentials)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any entity can deposit 32 ETH to queue a validator. The deposit data (pubkey, withdrawal credentials) is user-supplied and must be fully validated. No authentication is required beyond having the ETH.

trusted_external_entities.name: RPC Client via eth_config JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any client can query eth_config. Unauthenticated endpoint. Requests must be rate-limited and responses must not leak sensitive operational details beyond fork configuration.

trusted_external_entities.name: Malicious Actor via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Attacker can flood RPC endpoints for reconnaissance or DoS. All input is potentially malicious. Rate limiting and access control are required mitigations.

trusted_external_entities.name: Compromised Node via eth_config Response
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: eth_config RPC response (when querying reference nodes)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: A malicious node can return false configuration data. Responses must be cross-checked against multiple sources. No authentication of response content.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Sender via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated public endpoint. Transaction gasLimit, calldata (including ModExp precompile inputs), and all parameters are user-supplied and potentially crafted for DoS or exploitation. Full validation required including EIP-7825 gas cap enforcement.

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Node via P2P Network (devp2p)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P Network (devp2p block propagation, eth/69 protocol)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peer nodes are unauthenticated. They can broadcast blocks containing transactions with excessive gas limits or invalid data. All block data must be fully validated including per-transaction gas cap checks (EIP-7825).

trusted_external_entities.name: RPC Client Requesting Historical Data
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated client requesting historical blockchain data. After EIP-7927 history expiry, pre-merge data may not be locally available. Requests must be handled gracefully with appropriate error responses.

trusted_external_entities.name: Web Dapp via Browser postMessage/RPC
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Browser postMessage API (iframe) and popup-based eth_sendTransaction (EIP-107)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Web dapps are untrusted. They communicate via browser postMessage which relies on same-origin policy. Dapps can send arbitrary RPC requests; only whitelisted read-only methods should be allowed without user authorization. Transaction requests require explicit user approval via popup.

trusted_external_entities.name: End User via Browser Authorization Popup
trusted_external_entities.rationale: While the user is the intended authorizer, the popup interaction channel can be subject to UI spoofing or clickjacking. The system must ensure the popup accurately displays transaction parameters and cannot be manipulated by the dapp.

trusted_external_entities.name: Malicious Validator via P2P Network
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Archetypal CL attack vector. A malicious validator can propose invalid blocks, submit conflicting attestations, or attempt to manipulate the activation queue. All validator actions must be validated against protocol rules.

trusted_external_entities.name: Consensus Layer via Engine API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Authenticated via JWT. The CL directs the EL via Engine API, but payload content (blocks, transactions within them) must still be fully validated by the EL. Authentication provides channel integrity but not content trust.

trusted_external_entities.name: External Data Source for Pre-Merge History
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: e2store archives, Portal Network, EIP-7801 DevP2P protocol
trusted_external_entities.rationale: After EIP-7927 history expiry, pre-merge data may be sourced from external archives or decentralized networks. Data from these sources is untrusted and must be validated against known block hashes and transaction roots before being served or used.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Deposit data (pubkey, withdrawal credentials, amount) must be validated. Deposit amount must equal 32 ETH. Activation rate is bounded by EIP-7514 churn limit (max 8 per epoch).
Rate limiting must be enforced (recommended 1-second interval). Access should be restricted to trusted interfaces where possible. Response must reflect current chain head configuration.
All RPC requests must be validated for format, rate-limited, and access-controlled. eth_config must not expose sensitive operational details. DDoS mitigation required.
Configuration data from remote nodes must be cross-checked against multiple independent sources and the canonical specification. Single-source trust is insufficient.

Full transaction validation required: signature verification, nonce check, gas limit <= 16,777,216 (EIP-7825), sufficient balance, valid calldata. For ModExp precompile calls, gas pricing must follow EIP-7883 formula to prevent DoS.

All blocks must be fully validated: block header, transaction roots, and each transaction's gas limit must be <= 16,777,216 (EIP-7825). Blocks containing invalid transactions must be rejected. Peer eclipse attack mitigation required.
After EIP-7927 history expiry, pre-merge data requests must return appropriate error responses or redirect to alternate data sources. Must not cause node instability when data is unavailable.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Browser postMessage API (EIP-107 iframe and popup)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Read-only RPC methods must be whitelisted. State-modifying methods (eth_sendTransaction) require popup-based user authorization. eth_sign must be explicitly prohibited. Browser same-origin policy must be intact.

Popup must accurately display transaction parameters (from, to, gas, gasPrice). Account unlock window must be minimal (3 seconds). UI must not be spoofable by the dapp. Clickjacking protection required.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: P2P Network (Beacon gossip, block proposals, attestations)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: All validator actions must be validated against protocol rules. Invalid blocks must be rejected. Conflicting attestations must trigger slashing conditions. Activation churn limits (EIP-7514) bound the rate at which new validators (potentially attacker-controlled) can join.

JWT authentication must be verified for channel integrity. Despite authenticated channel, all payload content (block data, transactions) must be independently validated by the EL. EIP-7825 gas caps apply to transactions within Engine API payloads.

All externally sourced pre-merge data must be validated against known block hashes and transaction/receipt roots. Data integrity must be cryptographically verified before serving to RPC clients or using internally.
